learning: Iterations 7 to 10 show that controller gain (kp and kd) was the lever that moved the sharp tracks on this body. Iteration 10 (kd 0.75) is the best measured result, with the oval and s-bend both at 20/20 and slalom line-loss at 1.2.
notes: Final package: geometry held at the iteration 9 and 10 best values; controller set to the iteration 10 measured best (kd 0.75, kp 3.0). No untested gains are introduced for the final unseen-track race.
rationale: This is the final iteration, and the unseen track is scored once, so the package should be the best-measured platform rather than an untested variant. Geometry is held exactly at the Builder's iteration 11 values, which match iteration 9 and 10 (wheel_track 0.09 m, sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 0.015 m steps, y = 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.5 kg). Across iterations 7 to 10 the controller changes moved the sharp tracks, while geometry changes since iteration 4 were flat or negative. The controller is therefore set to the iteration 10 gains (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.75, base_speed 1.2, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction), which is the best measured result (700.7). Its oval finish rate (20/20, oscillation 0.21) and s-bend finish rate (20/20, line-loss 0.55) were both confirmed. Slalom remains 0/20 with line-loss 1.2, and iteration 9 (kd 0.6) had slalom line-loss 1.1, a difference that does not change the score much. I do not try an untested gain such as kd 0.9, because a stronger gain could push the jitter guard or the oval finish rate on the unseen shape without any race to check it. Expected result: about 700 on the development tracks, with the unseen track dependent on how well the controller generalises to a different curve shape.
